The Hyundai Stellar Four-Door Sedan Is a Virtual Proposal For a Very Different Kind of Aesthetics
9 photos
Photo: sshshhhhhh / Instagram
The good folks over at Hyundai are currently kicking off the latest design revolution dubbed ‘Art of Steel’ with major local and international models like the Avante, Bayon, or the best-selling Tucson, of course.
Alongside Kia, Hyundai has never been afraid to experiment – and the South Korean automaker has grown tremendously to the point of announcing one yearly sales record after another in major regions like the United States. From a little-known Asian carmaker to a global powerhouse was a long road, and the company traveled it with poise and confidence – especially in recent years.
As such, nobody is now surprised that Hyundai dares to innovate once again – they have proven to be a powerhouse in terms of EVs and even as a premium manufacturers through the Genesis brand subsidiary. This summer, at home in South Korea, they kicked off the new ‘ Art of Steel ’ design language together with the eighth-generation Hyundai Avante and Tucson.
The former was launched in June 2026 at the Busan International Mobility Show, and the latter, now reaching its fifth iteration (NX5), was first announced in August. The Hyundai Tucson reached international stardom at the 2026 Paris Motor Show in October when it was revealed in European specification alongside the smaller Hyundai Bayon, which is also following in its footsteps.
The fall automotive season continued for Hyundai with the launch of the international Elantra in November at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show (AutoMobility LA), with the 2027 Elantra and the 2028 Elantra Hybrid, seconded by the debuts in America of the all-new Tucson and Palisade XRT Pro alongside the brand-new Genesis G80 and GV80 Hybrid models.
Most likely, Hyundai will continue to showcase new models featuring the Art of Steel design language, although there was also some bad news – like the retirement of the larger Hyundai Sonata from the Australian market, where the new i30 Sedan (aka Elantra) will take its place. By the way, the Sonata is the largest sedan currently available in America, where it’s sold along with the compact Elantra.
Hyundai, on the other hand, has a gap in the lineup in terms of large passenger cars – they want you to go to Genesis to buy the larger sedans or jump into their crossover SUV lineup. Well, not everyone wants that – and just recently a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators found a solution to the predicament.
More precisely, the South Korean virtual artist Shin Sung-hwan, better known as ' sshshhhhhh ' on social media, has already cooked up Hyundai's potential next design language after 'Art of Steel' in their unofficial, hypothetical design project – and they also showcase a large sedan alongside it. Dubbed Hyundai Stellar, just like the model from 1983 to 1992, this is a minimalist, retro-modern four-door sedan model packing what look like recycled bumpers and rail-style front and rear LED lighting elements.
It also comes with an angular profile and massive alloy wheels, as well as classic four-door proportions and what looks like a leather-appointed interior. Quite obviously, if it ever existed, this model would place above the current Sonata. As for the powertrain, there are no obvious hints, which means it could be ICE, electrified, or a full EV.
So, what do you think? Should Hyundai think about building something like this – considering there’s a massive gap in the market in America when it comes to large sedans? Would this model represent a good alternative to the costlier German executive sedans or to the Dodge Charger sedan, for example? View this post on Instagram A post shared by 신성환 (@sshshhhhhh)
